blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Real-world speech is often partially observable: audio may be missing or corrupted by noise and competing speakers, while the speaker's lips remain visible. Recovering speech requires combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred from context. We introduce RML (Read My Lips), a collaborative method combining a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model. The lip reader provides articulation hypotheses, the language model uses context to resolve ambiguous or missing words, and the audio-visual generator reconstructs synchronized speech while preserving speaker identity. Since source reliability varies, RML generates multiple reconstructions and uses the available evidence to favor the most reliable ones. This allows RML to handle missing audio, strong interference, and poor visual evidence without manually defined thresholds. Quantitative and qualitative experiments across these conditions show the benefit of combining visual, acoustic, and linguistic signals.
blocks.zh: 现实世界的演讲往往有部分可观察性:音频可能会被噪音和相竞的扬声器所缺少或腐蚀,而扬声器的嘴唇则仍然能被看到. 恢复口语需要将可以听到的,看到的,从上下文推断出来的结合起来. 我们引入了RML(Read My Lips),一种结合了读唇器,语言模型,以及视听基因模型的合作方法. 相唇读取器提供发音假说,语言模型使用上下文来解决模棱两可或缺失的单词,而视听生成器则在保留演说者身份的同时重建同步语音. 由于源可靠性各有不同,RML生成了多个重建,并使用现有证据来偏好最可靠的重建. 这使得RML可以在没有手动定义阈值的情况下处理缺失的音频,强干扰,以及不良的视觉证据. 贯穿这些条件的定量和定性实验显示出将视觉、声学和语言信号结合起来的好处。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Imagine trying to follow a conversation at a crowded reception. Several people are speaking at once, music and background noise overwhelm parts of the speech, yet the person in front of you is clearly visible. Even when their voice becomes difficult to hear, their lip movements and the context of the conversation still provide clues about what they are saying. Similar situations arise in video calls with dropped audio, recordings made in noisy environments, archival footage with damaged sound, and film or content production where corrupted speech needs to be restored. In all these cases, recovering speech requires using whatever information remains available across the audio, video, and surrounding conversation.
blocks.zh: 想象一下在拥挤的招待会上 试图跟踪谈话 数人同时发言,音乐和背景噪音压倒了演讲的部分内容,然而你面前的人却明显可见. 即使他们的声音变得难以听到,他们的嘴唇动作和对话的背景仍然提供了他们所说的线索. 类似的情况也出现在视频通话中,这些视频带有空降的音频、在吵闹的环境中制作的录音、有受损声音的档案片段以及需要恢复腐败言论的电影或内容制作。 在所有这些情况下,恢复言论都要求使用音频、视频和周围对话中现有的任何信息。

blocks.en: More generally, real-world speech is often only partially observable. Background noise or competing speakers may obscure the audio, words may disappear due to recording or transmission failures, and the speaker’s mouth may be occluded or seen from a difficult viewpoint. We characterize these challenges along three dimensions, illustrated in Fig. 1 : acoustic noise , from clean speech to severe noise or competing speakers; missing words , from isolated words to large portions of an utterance; and visual readability , from a clear frontal face to difficult viewpoints, occlusions, or animated and generated speakers. These dimensions can vary independently, creating conditions in which no single modality is consistently reliable.
blocks.zh: 更一般地说,现实世界的言论往往只是部分可见. 背景噪音或相互竞争的发言者可能会遮掩音频,语言可能因录音或传输失败而消失,发言者的嘴可能被闭塞或从困难的角度看出来。 我们在图1中将这些挑战分为三个方面:声音噪音,从干净的演说到严重的演说者或相互竞争的演说者;话语缺失,从孤立的演说到一大部分的演说;视觉可读性,从清晰的正面到困难的观点,或动画和产生的演说者。 这些维度可以独立地变化,创造了没有一个单一模式始终可靠的条件.

blocks.en: Recovering speech under these conditions requires combining three complementary sources of evidence. Visual articulation provides information about the spoken sounds, but is inherently ambiguous because different phonemes can produce similar lip movements. Acoustic evidence , even when heavily corrupted, can provide cues about phonemes, timing, and speaker identity. Finally, linguistic context can resolve ambiguities using the surrounding reliable speech. For example, in “I ordered a — for lunch,” context strongly constrains the missing word. However, context alone is unreliable for names, numbers, or unexpected expressions. Effective restoration must therefore combine what can be seen , heard , and inferred .
blocks.zh: 在这些情况下恢复言论需要综合三个补充证据来源。 视觉表达提供了口语声音的信息,但本质上含糊不清,因为不同的电话可以产生相似的唇动. 声音证据,即使严重腐烂, 也可以提供提示 电话、时间和扬声器身份。 最后,语言背景可以利用周围的可靠言论解决模糊性. 例如,在“我订了午餐”中,“我订了午餐”一词就受到很大限制。 然而,仅上下文对于名称,数字,或意想不到的表达方式来说是不可靠的. 因此,有效恢复必须结合可以看到的、听到的和推断的。

blocks.en: Existing models provide complementary capabilities for these sources. Lip-reading models capture fine-grained visual articulation but struggle with ambiguous visemes, occlusion, and difficult viewpoints. Large language models use linguistic context to resolve ambiguities, but may favor plausible words over what was actually articulated. Audio-visual generative models can synthesize synchronized and speaker-consistent speech, but are not specialized for precise lip reading. Their complementary strengths motivate combining them rather than relying on any one model.
blocks.zh: 现有模式为这些来源提供了互补能力。 读唇模型捕捉到精细的视觉表达,但与模棱两可的模棱两可、隐蔽和困难的观点作斗争。 大语言模型使用语言上下文来解决含糊不清的问题,但可能倾向于用有说服力的词语而不是实际表述的词语。 视听的基因模型可以合成同步和说话一致的语音,但不专门用于精确的唇读. 它们相辅相成的长处促使它们结合在一起,而不是依赖任何一个模式。

blocks.en: We introduce RML ( Read My Lips ), a collaborative framework for audio-visual speech restoration. Given a video and potentially corrupted audio, a lip reader provides hypotheses about what is articulated, a language model reasons about what is plausible given the surrounding speech, and an audio-visual generative model reconstructs the final speech using these predictions together with the video and remaining acoustic evidence. Their relative importance naturally changes with the input: visual evidence dominates when audio is missing, context helps resolve ambiguous articulation, and remaining audio constrains pronunciation, timing, and speaker identity.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了RML(Read My Lips),这是视听语音恢复的合作框架. 鉴于一个视频和可能腐烂的音频,一个读唇者提供了对所表述内容的假设,一个语言模型说明鉴于周围的言语是可信的,一个视听基因模型利用这些预测以及视频和其余的声学证据来重建最后的言语. 它们的相对重要性随着输入而自然变化:视觉证据在音频缺失时占主导地位,上下文有助于解决模棱两可的表达,剩下的音频制约着发音,时间,和扬声器身份.

blocks.en:
RML thus formulates speech restoration as a multimodal inference problem (see Figure 1 ): the lip reader estimates what appears to be articulated , the language model reasons about what is plausible in context , and the audio-visual model determines how the recovered speech should sound and align with the video .
To adapt to different input conditions, RML generates multiple reconstructions using different component and audio conditions, scores their support from the observed audio and lip motion, and combines them through evidence-weighted minimum Bayes risk to favor the most reliable reconstructions. We evaluate RML across different levels of acoustic corruption, missing speech, and visual readability, demonstrating the benefit of combining these complementary sources of information.
blocks.zh:
RML因此将语音恢复表述为一种多式联运推论问题(见图1):读唇者估计了似乎被表述的内容,语言模型对上下文中合理内容的理由,视听模型决定了恢复的语音应如何发声并与视频一致。
为了适应不同的输入条件,RML使用不同的组件和音频条件生成多个重建,从所观测到的音频和唇动中计分他们的支持,并通过证据加权的最低贝叶斯风险将其组合起来,以利于最可靠的重建. 我们从不同层次的声学腐败、语言缺失和视觉可读性的角度来评价RML,表明将这些互补的信息来源结合起来的好处。

blocks.en: 2 Background: Phonemes and Visemes
blocks.zh: 2 背景:电话和视频

blocks.en:
Phonemes are the basic sound units that distinguish words in a spoken
language. For example, /p/, /b/, and /m/ are different phonemes.
Visemes are their visual counterparts: the mouth and lip configurations
seen when a person speaks. However, there is no one-to-one correspondence
between phonemes and visemes. Different sounds can produce nearly
identical mouth movements. For example, /p/, /b/, and /m/ all involve
closing the lips, making words such as pat , bat , and mat difficult to distinguish visually. This ambiguity makes
lip reading challenging even when the mouth is clearly visible.

blocks.en: 3 Related Work
blocks.zh: 3 相关工作

blocks.en: Lip reading has advanced through audio-visual self-supervised pretraining [ 50 ] and through training on large automatically labeled or pseudo-labeled corpora [ 35 , 22 , 23 ] . Native readers now also exist for languages other than English [ 36 ] . A recent line of work connects visual features to large language models. Some methods feed visual speech units or features directly into the LLM [ 57 , 4 ] ; others predict phonemes that the LLM then assembles into a sentence [ 54 ] . These models draw on the LLM’s knowledge of language. Used as lip readers, however, they see only the video and ignore the speech that is still audible around the words they must read. We use a lip reader as a black box that returns an N N -best list, and bring in the audible context at the next stage.
blocks.zh: 通过视听自导自演的预训[50],通过对自动标注或伪标注的大型蝎子的训练[35,22,23],唇读得到了进步. 现在除英语外,土著读者也存在. [36]. 最近的工作线将视觉特征与大型语言模型联系起来. 一些方法将视觉语音单元或特征直接输入LLM[57,4];其他方法预测LLM随后组装成句子[54]. 这些模型借鉴了LLM的语言知识. 他们只看到视频, 我们使用读唇器作为黑匣子,返回一个N-Best列表,并在下一阶段引入可听语语境.

blocks.en: Generative error correction trains an LLM to map the N N -best list of a speech recognizer to a corrected transcript [ 7 ] . Audio-visual variants condition this correction on lip features [ 19 ] or let the LLM combine separate audio and visual N N -best lists [ 27 ] . Our language model also combines a lip reader’s hypotheses with a transcript of the audio, but it decides what was said in a silenced span from the speech around it and the span’s duration.

blocks.en: Video-to-speech methods generate speech from a silent video. Early work trained one model per speaker [ 42 ] ; later methods work in the wild, through intermediate speech units [ 13 ] or resynthesis from audio-visual representations [ 25 ] . Several recent systems condition on text predicted by a lip reader. They pass it to a visual text-to-speech model [ 24 ] , use it to guide diffusion through a speech recognizer [ 56 ] , or attend to it together with the video and a reference of the speaker’s voice or face [ 12 , 33 ] . Lip-to-speech generation has also been shown to outperform audio-visual enhancement at very low signal-to-noise ratios [ 47 ] . All of these methods generate speech for the whole clip. None of them is designed to keep the original speech that survives in a partly damaged recording, or to reason over its words to recover the missing ones.
blocks.zh: 视频对语音方法从无声视频中生成语音. 早期工作培训了每个演讲者一个模型[42];后期方法在野外工作,通过中间语音单元[13]或从视听表达中进行合成[25]. 最近几个系统对一个读唇器预言的文字条件. 他们把它传递给视觉文字对语音模型[24],用它通过语音识别器指导传播[56],或者与视频和发言者的声音或表情的参考[12,33]一起关注.  Lip-to-speech 的生成也已被证明在信号-噪声比率非常低的情况下超过了视听增强[47]. 所有这些方法都为整个剪辑产生语音. 其中没有任何一个设计是将幸存下来的原声片保留在部分受损的录音中,或者为了找回失踪的声片而对其文字进行推理.

blocks.en: Audio-visual speech inpainting fills gaps of only up to 1.6 s in a recording from the speaker’s face, without a transcript [ 39 , 38 ] . Text-guided inpainting and editing models regenerate a marked span of a recording from its transcript while keeping the voice [ 3 , 32 , 41 , 55 ] . Zero-shot text-to-speech models clone a voice from a short prompt [ 11 , 5 ] . These models need the correct words as input and do not see the lips. They therefore cannot recover what was said, nor align the regenerated speech with the video. Our pipeline supplies the words from the lips and the context, and its generator attends to the video while it speaks them.
blocks.zh: 视听讲话的插画填补了从演讲者脸上录制的只长达1.6秒的空白,没有笔录[39、38]。 文字制导的涂装和编辑模型从记录稿中重新产生一段标记的录音,同时保留语音[3,32,41,55]. 零镜头的文字对语音模型克隆了来自一个短速的语音 [11, 5]. 这些模型需要正确的词作为输入,而不看到唇. 因此,他们无法收回所说的话,也无法使重新生成的演讲与视频保持一致。 我们的管道提供来自嘴唇和背景的文字,其生成者在讲视频时会关注视频。

blocks.en: Audio-visual enhancement and separation use the target speaker’s lip motion and face to isolate their voice from noise and competing speakers [ 1 , 16 , 18 , 45 ] . Generative variants resynthesize the speech instead of filtering it. They use a neural vocoder [ 37 ] or a diffusion model [ 14 ] , and the vocoder-based method extends enhancement to low signal-to-noise ratios. Audio-only enhancers [ 49 ] and restoration models that also take a transcript [ 28 ] cannot use the video. In our experiments, a prompt-based separation model [ 51 ] leaves heavily corrupted speech essentially unchanged. Enhancement methods are designed to recover a voice that is still present under the interference. Our generator also starts from the damaged track, but it is additionally conditioned on a transcript, which carries the content where the audible evidence disappears.
blocks.zh: 视听增强和分离利用目标发言者的嘴唇动作和面部动作,把他们的声音与噪音和相互竞争的发言者隔开[1、16、18、45]。 基因变体重新合成语音而不是过滤. 它们使用神经电极[37]或扩散模型[14],基于电极的方法将增强扩展到低信号对噪声比. 唯音增强器 [49] 和还原模型,也可以录制笔录 [28] 不能使用视频. 在我们的实验中,一个快速的分离模型[51] 使得严重腐败的言论基本上没有改变. 增强方法旨在恢复在干扰下仍然存在的声音. 我们的发电机也从受损的轨道开始,但附加附加条件的是记录誊本,其中包含可辨识的证据消失时的内容.

blocks.en: Open foundation models now generate video and audio jointly in one diffusion transformer with separate video and audio streams [ 21 ] . Built on the same backbone, Just-Dub-It [ 6 ] regenerates both the lips and the speech to dub a video into another language. Our task is complementary: the video is fixed and attended to, and only the speech is generated to match it.
blocks.zh: 开放基础模型现在在一个传播变压器中联合生成视频和音频,并有单独的视频和音频流[21]. Just-Dub-It[6] 将嘴唇和演讲都重现出来,将一段视频编成另一种语言。 我们的任务是互补的:视频是固定和处理的,只有演讲是制作来配合的.

blocks.en: 4.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 4.1 概览

blocks.en: RML combines visual, linguistic, and acoustic information via three complementary models ( Fig. 2 ). A lip reader R R (visual modality) produces a list of N N -best transcript hypotheses ℋ = ( h 1 , … , h N ) \mathcal{H}=(h_{1},\ldots,h_{N}) . A language model L L (context modality) combines these hypotheses with a Whisper transcript c c of a ~ \tilde{a} , in which silenced intervals, located by a simple energy threshold, are marked as gaps. Finally, an audio-visual generator G G (audio-visual modality) reconstructs the speech conditioned on V V , a ~ \tilde{a} , and the recovered text. The models communicate through plain text, making each replaceable; in particular, R R can be replaced by any visual speech recognizer without retraining L L or G G . We first describe each component of RML, and then introduce an adaptive selection process that determines how to use them based on the reliability of the available audio and visual evidence.
blocks.zh: RML通过三个互补模型(图2 )将视觉,语言,和声学信息结合起来. 一个读唇器R(视觉模式)生成一个N N - 最佳笔录假说H=(h 1,...,h N)\mathcal{(h_{1},\ldots,h_{N})列表. 一个语言模型L(context mode)将这些假说与一个~\tilde{a}的Whistory c c结合,其中以简单的能量阈值定位的沉默间隔被标记为空白. 最后,一个视听生成器G G(音频-视觉模式)重建了以V V为条件的语音,a ~\tilde{a},以及回收的文本. 模型通过纯文本进行交流,使每个模型可以替换;特别是R可以被任何视觉语音识别器所取代,而无需再培训L L或G G . 我们首先描述RML的每个组件,然后引入一个适应性选择过程,根据现有音频和视觉证据的可靠性决定如何使用它们.

blocks.en: 4.2 RML Framework
blocks.zh: 4.2 RML框架

blocks.en: Lip Reader as the Visual modality. When the audio is missing or corrupted, a lip reader provides complementary visual evidence of what was said. We use Auto-AVSR [ 35 ] for English and the CMU-MOSEAS readers of Ma et al. [36] for Spanish and French; the choice of reader is not critical, as swapping in USR 2.0 [ 23 ] without retraining any other component keeps the same gains ( Sec. 5.5 ). We use a pretrained visual speech recognizer that takes the mouth region of V V and returns the top N N transcripts using beam search. We process the full clip rather than only Ω \Omega , allowing the reader to use surrounding visual clues and its hypotheses to be aligned with the audible transcript downstream. We retain the N N -best list to provide alternative visual hypotheses to the language model, increasing the chance that the correct words are among the candidates.
blocks.zh: Lip Reader作为视觉模式. 当音频缺失或损坏时,一个读唇器会提供补充视觉证据来证明所说的话. 我们使用Auto-AVSR[35]对英语和CMU-MOSEAS对Ma等人的读者[36]对西班牙语和法语使用Auto-AVSR[35];读者的选择并不重要,因为互换在USR 2.0[23]中而不进行再培训,则保留了同样的收益(第5.5节)。 我们使用一个预先训练的视觉语音识别器,该识别器将V V的口腔区域,并使用光束搜索返回顶端的N N语录. 我们处理完整的剪辑,而不是只处理组合\Omega ,让读者使用周围的视觉线索,并且它的假说与下游的可声记录对齐. 我们保留N-Best列表,为语言模型提供替代的视觉假设,增加了正确词在候选词中的机会.

blocks.en:
Contextual Reasoning (Language Model). The language model (Gemma-4 12B [ 52 ] ) combines the visual hypotheses with the audible context to recover the transcript. We obtain the context c c by transcribing a ~ \tilde{a} with Whisper large-v3 [ 44 ] , marking detected silent intervals with placeholders and providing their durations; for noisy inputs, the transcript may instead contain incorrect or missing words. The model receives the audible context c c , a task tag ( <inpaint> if a silent gap is detected, <denoise> otherwise), and a list of candidate transcripts. For silenced inputs, the candidates are the lip reader’s N N -best hypotheses ℋ \mathcal{H} . For noisy inputs, where the audio still carries information, we interleave ℋ \mathcal{H} with the N N -best hypotheses of the audio-visual Auto-AVSR model [ 35 ] (or any AV recognizer) and add Whisper’s transcript of the noisy audio, removing duplicates. The model first chooses the most likely candidate and then uses the surrounding context to correct it and produce the final transcript.
We fine-tune the model on silenced and noisy clips with known word timings using the best candidate and reference transcript as supervision. To avoid dependence on a particular lip reader, training hypotheses are sampled from readers of different architectures and quality, including degraded-video variants, while the number of hypotheses is sampled uniformly between one and N N ; we use N = 10 N{=}10 throughout.
blocks.zh:
上下文推理(语言模型). 语言模型(Gemma-4 12B [52] )将视觉假说与可听的上下文结合起来,以收回笔录. 我们通过转录一个~\tilde{a}与Whisper大V3[44],用占位符检测到的无声间隔并提供其持续时间来获得上下文 c;对于吵闹的输入,记录稿可能包含不正确或缺失的单词. 该模型收到可调取的上下文c c,任务标记(如果检测到无声空白,则使用 " denoise " ),以及候选笔录清单。 对于沉默的输入,候选人是读唇语的N-最佳假设 H\ mathcal{H}。 对于噪音输入,如果音频仍然携带信息,我们将将H\ mathcal{H}与NN-音频Auto-AVSR模型最佳假说[35](或任何AV识别器)交互,并添加Whisper对噪音音频的记录,删除重复。 该模型首先选择最可能的候选人,然后利用周围的上下文进行校正,并产生最终的笔录.
我们用已知的文字计时方式, 为了避免对特定读唇器的依赖,培训假说从不同架构和质量,包括退化-视频变体的读者中抽取,而假说的数量则在1N和NN之间统一抽取;我们在整个过程中使用N=10N{=}10.

blocks.en:
AV modality and Speech Reconstruction. While any audio-visual generative model can be used, we use LTX-2.5 [ 21 ] because it is open-source and publicly available. LTX-2.5 is a diffusion transformer that jointly models video and audio latents with bidirectional attention and text conditioning.
We adapt the generator using dual canvas low-rank adapters [ 2 ] and use it only to generate speech: the video latents of V V provide visual clues, while the audio stream contains the input track as clean context followed by the target audio to be generated. A task tag, <inpaint> or <denoise> , optionally followed by a transcript, provides text conditioning. Together, these signals allow the generator to align speech with lip motion, preserve the speaker’s voice and audible speech, and reconstruct content that is silent or masked. The generated speech is synchronized with V V . Further training and implementation details are provided in the Appendix Appendix B .

AV模式和语音重建。 虽然任何视听的基因模型都可以使用,但我们使用LTX-2.5[21],因为它是开源的和公开的. LTX-2.5是一个扩散变压器,它联合对视频和音频潜伏物进行双向的注意和文本调制.

Data. We train on a small subset of TalkVid [ 9 ] : 6,509 of 4.8 s windows (English, Spanish and French) for the generator and 6,792 English windows for the language model, totaling fewer than 1,430 complete videos and 12 hours of speech. We test on unseen TalkVid videos, out-of-domain VoxMM [ 31 , 30 ] , Spanish and French videos, and a challenging set with side views, occlusions, animated characters, and generated speakers ( Tab. 1 ).
We corrupt each window by either removing 1–10 consecutive words or masking the full audio with babble, sound effects, or another speaker. Hyperparameters are tuned on 99 validation videos and fixed across test sets; Appendix Appendix A provides full details.

blocks.en: Metrics. We evaluate outputs based on their audible content. We transcribe generated audio with Whisper large-v3 [ 44 ] and compare it with the reference. For silenced speech, we report exact span recovery and word accuracy , scoring only examples that Whisper correctly transcribes before corruption. For noisy speech, we report window-level WER. Statistical significance is determined using 95% paired bootstrap intervals over source videos. The intervals are given in Appendix Sec. D.1 , a check with a second recognizer in Appendix Sec. D.6 , and the naturalness, speaker identity and lip synchronization of the generated speech in Appendix Appendix E .

blocks.en: Baselines. To our knowledge, no existing method combines lip reading, linguistic context and the surviving audio to restore both silenced and noisy speech, adapting to whichever source is reliable for each input. We therefore evaluate word-recovery accuracy on both tasks against the closest baselines. For silenced speech, we compare with lip/AV recognizers (Auto-AVSR [ 35 ] , USR 2.0 [ 23 ] , Llama-AVSR [ 4 ] ), speech editors given the missing words and location (F5-TTS [ 11 ] , VoiceCraft [ 41 ] , AlignDiT [ 12 ] ), and LipVoicer [ 56 ] . For noisy speech, we compare with audio restoration (DeepFilterNet3 [ 49 ] , Sidon [ 40 ] ) and audio-visual separation (VisualVoice [ 18 ] , SAM Audio [ 51 ] ).
blocks.zh: 基线。 据我们所知,没有一种现有方法将唇读、语言背景和幸存的音频结合起来,以恢复沉默和吵闹的语音,适应每种输入都可靠的来源。 因此,我们对照最接近的基线来评价这两项任务的文字恢复准确性。 对于沉默的演讲,我们与唇语/AV识别器(Auto-AVSR [35],USR 2.0 [23],Llama-AVSR [4]),语音编辑,考虑到缺失的词和位置(F5-TTS [11],VoiceCraft [41],AlignDIT [12]),以及LipVoicer [56]. 对于吵闹的言论,我们比较了音频修复(DeepFilterNet3 [49],Sidon [40])和视听分离(VisualVoice [18],SAM Audio [51]).

blocks.en: Table 2 shows that our method achieves the best results across all word-accuracy and span-recovery metrics, whether using Auto-AVSR or the stronger USR 2.0 as the lip reader. With Auto-AVSR, it exactly recovers 39.3 % 39.3\% of silenced spans, compared with 30.7 % 30.7\% for Auto-AVSR alone, already on par with or above the stronger USR 2.0 itself, and with USR 2.0 this rises to 43.8 % 43.8\% , 8 points above USR 2.0 alone. Notably, speech editors such as F5-TTS and AlignDiT are given both our language model’s transcript and the span location, whereas our generator must infer the span itself, yet still performs better. These gains show that our method improves over the lip readers and benefits from jointly using visible lips and surrounding audible speech.

blocks.en: 5.2 Restoring Noisy and Overlapping Speech
blocks.zh: 5.2 恢复噪音和重叠发言

blocks.en: Table 3 reports WER over the full 4.8 s speech windows, averaged across the different noise conditions; results broken down by individual test set are provided in Appendix Sec. D.3 . On average, our pipeline reduces WER from 69.0 % 69.0\% for the noisy input to 25.5 % 25.5\% , outperforming all baselines. Audio-only methods struggle under strong noise, while video-only methods discard useful speech. AV recognizers such as USR 2.0 (AV) benefit when the audio remains less noisy and mostly informative: at − 5 -5 dB babble, USR 2.0 (AV) comes closest to ours because the relatively mild noise still allows the audio to reveal much of the speech. As corruption increases, this advantage disappears; at − 10 -10 dB babble, our method substantially outperforms all AV recognizers. Under a competing talker, VisualVoice, a model built specifically for speaker separation, comes level with ours.

blocks.en: 5.3 Adapting to Audio Corruption
blocks.zh: 5.3 适应音频腐败

blocks.en: Different types and levels of corruption make different signals more reliable, but at test time we do not know which configuration is best for a given input. Our method therefore considers all six configurations and uses their evidence scores to select the most reliable output. To test this, we use the same test windows and vary both the corruption and its duration: babble at − 5 -5 , − 10 -10 , or − 20 -20 dB, or silence, affects one word, four words, or the whole clip. We also include clean clips. This gives 1,421 TalkVid and 1,998 VoxMM samples, evaluated using WER over the full window.
blocks.zh: 不同的腐败类型和程度使得不同的信号更加可靠,但在测试时我们不知道哪种配置最适合给定输入. 因此,我们的方法考虑了所有六个配置,并利用它们的证据分数来选择最可靠的输出. 为了测试这一点,我们使用同样的测试窗口,并同时改变腐败及其持续时间:bulble at − 5 - 5, − 10 - 10, 或 − 20 - 20 dB, 或沉默,影响一个字,四个字,或整个片段. 我们还包括干净的片段。 这使1 421个TalkVid和1 998个VoxMM样本在全窗口上使用WER进行评估。

blocks.en: Fig. 4 (Bottom) shows how our method changes its selection as the audio becomes less reliable. For clean clips, it almost always keeps the audio. As the corruption becomes stronger and covers more of the clip, it increasingly selects configurations that replace the corrupted audio with silence. For example, when the whole clip is corrupted by − 20 -20 dB babble (right diagram), it removes the audio for 88% of the clips, and the voice is then inferred from the speaker’s appearance rather than taken from the recording (Appendix Appendix E ). Importantly, the method is not given the noise level or corrupted region; it makes this decision from the evidence scores. The audio evidence drops from ∼ 80 \sim 80 for clean clips to ∼ 3 \sim 3 at − 20 -20 dB, giving more weight to the transcript and visual evidence.
blocks.zh: 图4 (Bottom) 显示随着音频的可靠性降低,我们的方法如何改变其选择. 对于干净的片段,它几乎总是保留音频. 随着腐败变得更加强大并覆盖更多的剪辑,它越来越多地选择以沉默取代腐败音频的配置. 例如,当整个剪辑被 − 20 - 20 dB bable (右图) 腐蚀时,它会删除88%的剪辑的音频,然后从演讲者的外表推断出声音,而不是从录音中提取(附录E ). 重要的是,该方法没有给予噪音水平或腐败地区;它根据证据得分作出这一决定。 音频证据从 ^ 80\sim 80作为干净的片段下降到 − 3\sim 3 at − 20 - 20 dB,使记录和视觉证据更具份量.

blocks.en: Fig. 4 (Top) shows the benefit of this selection. The black curve shows our adaptive selection, which matches or improves on the best fixed configuration across the different corruption conditions. No single fixed configuration works best across all corruption levels. The generator alone works well when the noise is mild, but becomes unreliable under severe corruption, reaching over 100% WER when the whole clip is corrupted at − 20 -20 dB. Using a transcript helps, but configurations that keep the corrupted audio still suffer from the noise. By choosing whether to keep or remove the audio based on its reliability, our method reaches 49.8 % 49.8\% WER in this difficult case. Across all conditions, adaptive selection achieves 23.1 % 23.1\% WER, compared with 26.4 % 26.4\% for always using R → G R\rightarrow G , 26.8 % 26.8\% for R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G , 40.8 % 40.8\% for the generator alone, and 49.1 % 49.1\% for the lip reader.

blocks.en: 5.4 Hard-to-Read Lips
blocks.zh: 5.4 难读唇

blocks.en: Here we test whether our method remains robust when lip reading is unreliable by detecting weak visual evidence and shifting toward more reliable sources, such as language and audio. We collect 44 44 English windows from 23 23 scenes (e.g., movies, animation and generated videos) in which the mouth is hard or impossible to read because of side views, occlusions or animated characters. On these windows we silence spans of k = 1 k=1 , 3 and 5 words (116 verified cuts) and apply the noise conditions of Tab. 3 (220 noisy samples), and compare with baselines on both tasks ( Tab. 4 ).
blocks.zh: 在这里,我们通过检测弱视证据和转向语言和音频等更可靠的来源,检验在唇读不可靠时,我们的方法是否仍然有力。 我们从23场23场景(如电影,动画和生成的视频)中收集44个44个英语窗口,其中由于侧面视图,隔离或动画角色,嘴部很难或无法阅读. 在这些窗口上,我们沉默的时间跨度为k=1 k=1,3和5个字(116个经核实的剪切),并适用Tab 3(220个吵闹样本)的噪音条件,并与两个任务的基线进行比较(Tab 4 )。

blocks.en: Our method scores highest on both tasks, recovering three times more silenced spans than its own lip reader. When the lips are unreliable, it relies more on the other components: the language model predicts the missing words from context, and the generator speaks them in the speaker’s voice. This also explains why speech editors given our language model transcript perform closest to our method on silenced speech. Importantly, our method is not told when lip reading fails; the language model and the surviving audio compensate for what the lips cannot show. Lip-reading baselines use only the lips ( V V ) for silenced speech and both lips and audio ( A ​ V AV ) for noisy speech, but still perform much worse. Some baselines (marked ∗ ) require a detected face and fail when the mouth is never visible, so we score them only on the windows they can process.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法在两项任务上都得分最高,恢复了比自己的读唇器多三倍的消音间隔。 当唇不可靠时,它更依赖于其他组件:语言模型从上下文中预测缺失的单词,生成器用扬声器的声音来说话. 这也解释了为什么语言编辑给我们的语言模型笔录 与我们沉默的演讲方法最接近。 重要的是,在唇读失败时,我们的方法不会被告知;语言模型和幸存的音频可以补偿唇不能显示的东西。 唇读基线只使用唇(V V)进行沉默的语音,同时使用唇音和音频(A V AV)进行喧闹的语音,但表现仍然糟糕得多. 一些基线(标记为*)需要检测到的面孔,当嘴永远看不到时会失败,所以我们只在他们可以处理的窗口上进行计分.

blocks.en: 5.5 Generalization
blocks.zh: 5.5 概论

blocks.en: Since the components communicate via text, R R can be replaced with no retraining. With USR 2.0 as R R under the same selection ( Tabs. 2 and 3 ), our method improves on both tasks: a stronger lip reader directly yields a stronger pipeline, while L L and G G provide further gains. Interestingly, even with Auto-AVSR as R R , our method remains the second-best overall, behind only our version with USR 2.0. This shows that the gains come from the framework itself and remain strong across different lip readers. The same holds across languages ( Tab. 5 b): with a Spanish or French lip reader as R R , and L L and G G unchanged, the pipeline improves exact recovery over the lip reader by a third.
blocks.zh: 由于组件通过文本进行交流,RR可以被替换为不进行再培训. 以USR 2.0作为R在相同的选择下(Tabs. 2和3),我们的方法在这两个任务上都有改进:一个更强的读唇器直接产生更强的管道,而LL和GG则提供了进一步的收益. 有趣的是,即使Auto-AVSR是R, 我们的方法仍然是第二好的整体, 这表明,这些成果来自框架本身,在不同唇形读物之间仍然强劲。 不同语言的情况也是如此(Tab. 5b):以西班牙语或法语的唇读器为R,LL和G不变,管道使唇读器的准确恢复率提高了三分之一。

blocks.en: 5.6 Ablations
blocks.zh: 5.6 拖欠款项

blocks.en:
Tab. 5 ablates the components of our pipeline to demonstrate the contribution of each model. First, giving the lip reader’s N N -best hypotheses to the language model, together with the audible context, gives a much better transcript than the lip reader alone ( R → L R\rightarrow L against R R ). Second, the generator G G is more than a renderer. If G G simply spoke the input text like a text-to-speech model, the lips it sees would not matter. Instead, with the same transcript but mismatched lips, it performs significantly worse (Appendix Sec. D.5 ).
Third, the language model matters most for long gaps: without it ( R → G R\rightarrow G ) the pipeline loses spans at every length, and for seven to ten missing words the full pipeline recovers 42% more spans than the lip reader.
blocks.zh:
Tab. 5将输油管的部件减少,以显示每个模型的贡献。 首先,给语言模型提供读唇的N-最佳假设,加上可听语的上下文,可以提供比读唇的读者要好得多的文字记录(R → L R\rightarrow L at r R ). 其次,发电机GG不仅仅是一个渲染器. 如果GG简单地用文字对语音模型来表达输入文本,那么它看到的唇就不重要了. 相反,使用相同的记录,但嘴唇不匹配,其表现则严重恶化(附录Sec.D.5 )。
第三,语言模型对于长期差距最为重要:没有它(R → G R\rightarrow G ) 管道会失去每个长度的跨度,对于7到10个缺失的字,整个管道会比读唇器恢复42%的跨度.

blocks.en: No fixed configuration is best everywhere. The language model helps on silenced speech, but on noisy speech the audio still carries most of the words, and R → G R\rightarrow G does better without it. Our selection does not know which case it is in, yet it gives the lowest error on noisy speech and is close to the best on silenced speech. The only exception is the silenced hard set, where the difference is not significant. Here the lips cannot be read, making the visual evidence used by the selection unreliable and sometimes causing it to choose an output that follows the lip reader’s wrong prediction.
blocks.zh: 没有固定的配置是任何地方最好的. 语言模型有助于沉默的语音,但在吵吵的语音中,音频仍然携带着大部分的单词,没有它,R → G R\rightarrow G做的更好. 我们的选择并不知道它属于哪一种情况,然而它却给吵闹的演讲带来最小的错误,并且对沉默的演讲也接近最佳. 唯一的例外是沉默的硬套,其中差异并不显著。 在这里,唇不能被读取,使得选择所使用的视觉证据不可靠,有时导致它选择一个遵循唇读器错误预测的输出.

blocks.en: One may expect the language model to read better if it saw the lips directly rather than through a lip reader’s hypotheses. We test this with a small head that reads AV-HuBERT [ 50 ] mouth features and passes its viseme posteriors to L L as soft input tokens, trained jointly with L L . The model does rely on the head, since features from another clip lower exact recovery by 22.8 points on the validation set, yet the head brings no gain on any test set and loses spans where the lip features are least reliable ( Tab. 5 c). The ranked hypotheses thus carry the visual information L L needs.
blocks.zh: 如果语言模型直接看到嘴唇,而不是通过读唇者的假说,人们可能会期望语言模型读得更好。 我们用一个读AV-HuBERT[50]口腔特征的小头来测试这个,并将它的粘膜后部传递给LL作为软输入符号,与LL联合训练. 该模型确实依赖于头部,因为另一个片段的特征在验证集上降低了22.8分的精确恢复,然而头部却在任何测试集上都没有收获,在唇部特征最不可靠的地方会失去跨度(Tab. 5 c). 因此,排名的假设带有视觉信息LL需要。

blocks.en: To check that every term of the selection rule ( Eq. 3 ) is needed, we remove them one at a time. Each helps in at least one setting, and removing any term gives no significant improvement in any setting (Appendix Appendix C ).
blocks.zh: 为了检查选择规则(Eq. 3)的每个术语都需要,我们一次去掉一个. 每个词至少都有助于一个设置,删除任何术语都不会显著改善任何设置(附录C)。

blocks.en: Given the true transcript, G G recovers 96.6% of the silenced spans on TalkVid and VoxMM, more than any speech editor given the same text. Under noise, it roughly halves the WER, bringing it close to that of the clean recordings; the hard set shows the same pattern. This suggests that most remaining errors come from the transcript and not the generator, making the lip reader and language model the main components to improve.
blocks.zh: GG在TalkVid和VoxMM上恢复96.6%的消音间隔, 在噪音下,它大致将WER减半,使其接近干净的录音;硬盘显示相同的图案. 这表明,大多数剩余的错误来自抄本而不是生成器,使得读唇器和语言模型成为需要改进的主要组成部分.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en: We introduced Read My Lips, a method for recovering speech by bringing together lip reading, language understanding, and audio-visual generation. This work points to an intriguing opportunity made possible by recent advances in language and audio-visual models: we can now combine their complementary abilities to recover information that each model alone may miss. Words that are unclear from the lips may become clear from the conversation, and speech buried in noise may still be revealed by the speaker’s mouth movements. This is similar to human perception, focusing on clearest sensory cues based on the situation. Together, these clues can make an otherwise unintelligible recording understandable again.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Read My Lips,一种通过将唇读、语言理解和视听生成结合起来来恢复语音的方法。 这项工作表明,语言和视听模式最近的进展提供了令人感兴趣的机会:我们现在可以把它们的补充能力结合起来,以恢复每个模式可能遗漏的信息。 嘴唇上的言语可能从谈话中变得清晰,被噪音掩埋的言语仍然可能由演讲者的口腔动作所揭示. 这与人类的认知相似,根据情况注重最清晰的感官提示. 这些线索加在一起,可以让本来无法理解的录音再次被理解.

blocks.en: Making this collaboration work requires knowing when to trust each source. More information is not always better: severely corrupted audio can mislead the model, while ignoring it can improve recovery. Similarly, a language model can produce a convincing sentence without knowing whether it was actually spoken, and lip reading can become unreliable when the mouth is unclear or occluded. The challenge is that at inference time, it is not known which of these sources is reliable for a given input. Their reliability must therefore be judged from the available evidence. This creates an opportunity to combine the language model’s ability to reason about speech with the evidence in the audio and lip motion, relying on each source when it is informative and less when it is not.
blocks.zh: 要使这种合作发挥作用,需要知道何时可以信任每个来源。 更多信息并不总是更好:严重损坏的音频可以误导模型,而忽略它可以改善恢复. 同样地,一个语言模型可以在不知道是否实际是口语的情况下产生令人信服的句子,唇读在口语不清或被吞噬时会变得不可靠. 挑战在于,在推论时,不知道这些来源中哪一个对某项投入是可靠的。 因此,必须根据现有证据判断其可靠性。 这创造了一种机会,将语言模型对言论的理性能力与音频和口语动作中的证据结合起来,在信息丰富时依赖每个来源,而在信息缺乏时则较少。

blocks.en: What remains unsolved is also encouraging. Once the words are correct, the generator can reconstruct the speech with high accuracy. As speech generation becomes increasingly capable, recovering the correct words becomes the central challenge. The emergence of strong language and audio-visual models makes this a timely direction to explore: how far can we go in recovering what was said by combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred?
blocks.zh: 仍未解决的问题也令人鼓舞。 一旦文字正确,生成器可以高精度地重建语音. 随着语音生成能力日益增强,恢复正确的词语成为中心挑战. 强大的语言和视听模式的出现,使这个方向成为一个及时的探索方向:我们如何通过综合能够听到、看到和推断的东西来恢复所说的话?

blocks.en: The hard set contains English windows in which the mouth is difficult or impossible to read because the speaker is viewed from the side, the mouth is hidden by a hand or an object, or the speaker is animated or generated. Twenty-eight windows come from generated videos, and the other 16 from films and animation. As one measure of visual availability, we run a face landmark detector on every frame. It finds the mouth in every frame of 32 windows, in some frames of 5, and in no frame of the remaining 7.
blocks.zh: 硬套包含英语窗口,由于扬声器从侧面查看,嘴被手或物体隐藏,或者扬声器是动画或生成,所以嘴部难以或无法读取. 28个窗口来自生成的视频,其他16个来自电影和动画. 作为可视性的一个衡量标准,我们在每个帧上运行一个面部标志性的探测器. 它在每个32个窗框中发现口,在某些窗框中是5个,在其余7个窗框中没有.

blocks.en: All hyperparameters, including the temperature T T of the selection, are chosen on a validation set of English TalkVid windows, each from a different video, that shares no video with the training or test sets.
blocks.zh: 所有超参数,包括选择时的温度T T,都选在一套验证的英语TalkVid窗口上,每个窗口来自不同的视频,这些视频与训练或测试集没有共享视频.

blocks.en: A.2 Corruptions
blocks.zh: A.2 腐败

blocks.en: For each window and each k k from 1 to 10, we seek one span of k k consecutive words using forced-alignment timings. We exclude spans that begin or end with a stop word or filler, whose boundaries the aligner places least reliably. At least one word must remain audible on either side, keeping the span away from window edges where words may be truncated. We set the audio to zero from 80 ms before the span’s first word to 80 ms after its last, stopping 20 ms short of neighboring words. We reject a position if this interval leaves part of a span word audible or if a word at the span edge lasts less than 80 ms, indicating a faulty alignment. Among valid positions, we prefer one containing the word around which the window was cut, then the one nearest the window center. A window yields no cut for a given k k if no position meets these rules ( Tab. 6 ). For TalkVid, and for Spanish and French, the transcripts and word timings come from WhisperX. For VoxMM we use the transcripts and word timings of the LRS-VoxMM release unchanged. Where a manual review corrected a reference, the corrected words take the time span of the words they replace, and cuts that cover only part of a corrected run are removed.
blocks.zh: 每个窗口和每个kk从1到10,我们利用强制对齐的时间来寻找一个 kk连续单词的跨度. 我们排除了以句号或填充符开始或结束的跨度,其连接符位置最不可靠。 在两侧,至少必须保持一个字的可读性,使字段远离可能截断的窗口边缘。 我们把音频设定为零, 从第一个字之前的80ms到最后一个字之后的80ms, 我们拒绝一个位置,如果这个间隔留下了部分跨度词的可听性,或者如果一个字在跨度边缘的长度小于80毫秒,表明一个错误的对齐。 在有效位置中,我们更喜欢一个包含窗口被剪掉的字,然后是离窗口中心最近的一个。 如果某个 k k 的位置不符合这些规则, 窗口则不产生切数( Tab. 6 )。 对于 TalkVid , 西班牙语和法语则来自 WhisperX 。 对于VoxMM,我们使用 LRS-VoxMM 发行的文字记录和文字计时,没有改变. 如果人工审查纠正了引用,则更正后的字段需要其替换的字段的时长,只涵盖更正运行部分内容的删减将被删除。

blocks.en: For babble, training uses DEMAND cafeteria noise [ 53 ] from microphone channels 1 to 12. For testing, we mix each full window with a variety of interference, to examine how the method behaves under different conditions. The main evaluation has five conditions. Two use DEMAND cafeteria babble from the held-out channels 13 to 16, at − 10 -10 and − 5 -5 dB. Two use VGGSound environmental sounds [ 8 ] at − 5 -5 dB, from test clips of the nine classes used in training or from three held-out classes (church bell, sneezing, train horn). The fifth is a competing speaker at − 5 -5 dB, drawn from another video in the same test set. Section D.2 repeats the babble evaluation with two independent sources, the DEMAND restaurant scene and a mixture of six other speakers, and our WER does not change significantly. We set the signal-to-noise ratio using the root-mean-square levels of the clean window and the noise.
blocks.zh: 对于bulble,训练使用从麦克风1频道到12频道的DEAND自助餐厅噪音[53]. 为了测试,我们把每个全窗口与各种干扰混合,以检查方法在不同条件下的表现. 主要评价有五个条件. 两次使用来自13至16频道的DEAND自助餐厅泡泡,时间为−10-10和−5-5分贝。 两次使用VGGSound环境声[8],时间为 − 5-5 dB,来自训练中使用的9个班的测试片段或3个停课班(教堂钟、喷嚏、火车喇叭)。 第五个是来自同一套测试中的另一段视频, D.2节用两个独立来源重复了Babble评价,即DEAND餐厅场景和另外六位演讲者的混合,我们的WER没有显著变化. 我们利用干净窗口的根-正方位和噪音来设定信号-噪声比.

blocks.en: For Sec. 5.3 , we vary both the strength and extent of corruption. Babble at − 5 -5 , − 10 -10 or − 20 -20 dB, or silence, affects one word, four words or the whole window, and clean windows are included. The resulting grid contains 1,421 TalkVid and 1,998 VoxMM samples, and Tab. 12 reports every condition. We construct the validation grid in the same way from validation windows.
blocks.zh: 对于第5.3条,腐败的力量和程度各不相同。 babble at − 5 - 5, − 10 - 10 或 − 20 - 20 dB,或沉默,影响一个字,四个字或整个窗口,包含干净的窗口. 由此形成的网格包含1,421 TalkVid和1,998 VoxMM样本,Tab. 12报告每个条件. 我们用同样的方式从验证窗口中构建验证网格.

blocks.en: A.3 Scoring and statistics
blocks.zh: A.3 分红和统计

blocks.en: Every output is transcribed over the whole window with Whisper large-v3 [ 44 ] , and the transcript is aligned with the reference after text normalization. A silenced cut counts as exactly recovered when every silenced word is matched in place and no word is inserted inside the span. The word accuracy is the percentage of silenced words that are matched in place. Methods that only produce text, such as the lip readers, are scored on their text with the same alignment.
blocks.zh: 每个输出都用Whisper大V3[44]在全窗口上转录,记录稿在文本正常化后与引用一致. 当每个沉默的字都匹配,而且间距内没有插入任何字时,一个沉默的切数算作完全恢复。 字的准确性是对应的沉默字的百分比. 只产生文本的方法,如读唇器,在他们的文本上以相同的对齐进行打分.

blocks.en: Whisper can itself misrecognize disfluencies, ambiguously written numbers, or words truncated at a window edge. To avoid counting such errors as restoration failures, we score a silenced cut only when Whisper transcribes its missing words exactly from the original, undamaged audio. These verified cuts account for 91% of TalkVid cuts and 85% of VoxMM cuts ( Tab. 6 ). For noisy speech, we report whole-window word error rate averaged over windows. It can exceed 100% when an output inserts many words, for example by including a competing speaker.
blocks.zh: 微声本身可以错误地识别出疏漏,模糊的写法数字,或者在窗口边缘截断单词. 为了避免将错误计算为修复失败,我们只有在Whisper从原始的、未损坏的音频中准确记录其缺失的字句时才得分。 这些经核实的切数占TalkVid切数的91%和VoxMM切数的85%(图6)。 对于吵闹的言论,我们报告整个窗口的字数错误率平均在窗口上。 当一个输出插入许多单词时,它可以超过100%,例如通过包含一个相竞的扬声器.

blocks.en: Because cuts and windows from the same video are correlated, we compute 95% percentile confidence intervals with a paired bootstrap over source videos, or over scenes for the hard set, using at least 2,000 resamples. We call a difference significant when its interval excludes zero.
blocks.zh: 因为来自同一视频的剪切和窗口是相互关联的, 我们计算95%的置信间隔, 上面有一个对齐的靴子圈, 上面是源视频, 或外景上的硬盘, 至少使用2000个复刻。 我们称其间距排除零时差异很大。

blocks.en: A.4 Baselines
blocks.zh: A.4 基线

blocks.en: Every baseline runs with its official code and checkpoint on the same windows as our method and is scored by the same scorer.
blocks.zh: 每个基准都用官方代码和检查点 和我们的方法一样 由同一个计分员打分

blocks.en: Auto-AVSR [ 35 ] , USR 2.0 [ 23 ] and Llama-AVSR [ 4 ] produce only text. For silenced speech they read the lips alone. For noisy speech we run each from the lips alone (V) and from the lips together with the noisy audio (AV). The visual Auto-AVSR model is also our lip reader R R .
blocks.zh: Auto-AVSR [35],USR 2.0 [23]和Llama-AVSR [4]只产生文本. 对于沉默的言论,他们只读唇。 对于吵闹的演说,我们各自从嘴唇(V)和嘴唇与吵闹的声音(AV)一起运行。 视觉Auto-AVSR模型也是我们的读唇器R R.

blocks.en: F5-TTS [ 11 ] and VoiceCraft [ 41 ] fill a marked audio span with supplied words in the speaker’s voice, and AlignDiT [ 12 ] also conditions on the lips. Each editor receives our language model’s transcript, the same text available to our generator, as well as the silenced span’s location, which our method must infer from the input. We score the output returned by each editor’s official inference code. Pasting only AlignDiT’s generated span back into the input changes its exact recovery from 35.7% to 36.6% without affecting any comparison. With the lip reader’s best hypothesis in place of the language model’s transcript, F5-TTS and AlignDiT recover 30.3% and 31.4% of spans exactly, about five points fewer than with L L ’s transcript ( Tab. 13 a).
blocks.zh: F5-TTS [11] 和VoiceCraft [41] 填充一个有标记的音频间距,在演讲者的声音中填充有供应的单词,AlignDIT [12] 在嘴唇上也附加条件. 每个编辑都收到我们语言模型的笔录, 和生成器的文本一样, 我们按每个编辑器的官方推论代码对输出进行评分。 仅粘贴 AlignDIT 生成的数据可以追溯到输入时,其确切的回收率从35.7%变为36.6%,不影响任何比较。 F5-TTS和AlignDIT完全恢复了30.3%和31.4%的长度,比LL的笔录少了大约5个百分点(Tab.13a)。

blocks.en: LipVoicer [ 56 ] synthesizes the speech of the whole window from the video, guided by its own lip reader, and ignores the input audio. On noisy speech, AlignDiT receives the lip reader’s best hypothesis and, as a reference for the voice, a clean recording of the same speaker from another window. It also ignores the noisy input, so its error does not depend on the noise condition.
blocks.zh: LipVoicer[56]从视频中合成了整个窗口的语音,由自己的读唇器指导,忽略了输入音频. AlignDiT收到唇语读者的最佳假设, 它也忽略了噪音输入,因此其错误并不取决于噪音条件.

blocks.en: DeepFilterNet3 [ 49 ] and Sidon [ 40 ] process the noisy audio alone. VisualVoice [ 18 ] separates the target speaker using their face. SAM Audio [ 51 ] is prompted either with the text “speech” or with the masked video of the target speaker.
blocks.zh: DeepFilterNet3 [49]和西顿[40]单独处理吵闹的音频. VisualVoice [18] 将目标扬声器用脸分开. SAM Audio [51] 要么用“speech”的文字,要么用目标扬声器的蒙面录像。

blocks.en: Table 7 : What each method receives. Span : the location of the silenced interval. Transcript : a transcript supplied from outside the method, from our lip reader ( R R ) or our language model ( L L ). Voice : a clean recording of the speaker from another window. ∗ A text description of the target sound, not a transcript.
blocks.zh: 表7:每种方法都收到什么。 Span : 沉默间隔的位置. 笔录:从方法之外,从我们的读唇器(R R)或语言模型(L L )提供的笔录。 声音:从另一个窗口对扬声器进行干净的录音. 页:1 对目标声音的文字描述,而不是笔录.

blocks.en: Table 7 specifies the inputs available to each method. Our method receives the video and the damaged audio. The speech editors additionally receive the silenced span’s location and our language model’s transcript. For noisy speech, AlignDiT also receives a clean recording of the speaker. These additional inputs should be considered when interpreting the comparisons.
blocks.zh: 表7列明了每种方法可用的投入。 我们的方法接收到视频和损坏的音频。 此外,演讲编辑还收到消音段的位置和我们语言模型的记录。 对于吵闹的演讲,AlignDIT也收到一个发言者的干净录音. 在解释比较时应考虑这些额外投入。

blocks.en: Face-dependent methods cannot process every window. On TalkVid and VoxMM, VisualVoice covers 1,245 of the 1,365 noisy windows and AlignDiT covers 1,315. Coverage is lower on the hard set, where USR 2.0 and Llama-AVSR process about three quarters of the cuts and windows, and VisualVoice fewer than half of the noisy windows ( Tab. 14 ). For each such baseline, we compute both scores on the cuts or windows it covers.
blocks.zh: 依赖面部的方法不能处理每个窗口. 在TalkVid和VoxMM上,VisualVoice覆盖了1,365个吵闹的窗口中的1,245个,AlignDiT覆盖了1,315个. 其中USR 2.0和Llama-AVSR处理大约四分之三的切口和窗口, 对于每一个这样的基线,我们计算它覆盖的切片或窗户的得分。

blocks.zh: 附 录 B

blocks.en: B.1 Models and training
blocks.zh: B.1 模式和培训

blocks.en: The lip reader R R applies visual Auto-AVSR [ 35 ] to mouth crops from the whole window. Beam search returns its N = 10 N=10 best distinct transcripts. For Spanish and French, we use the readers of Ma et al . [ 36 ] instead. Whisper large-v3 transcribes a ~ \tilde{a} to provide audible context c c . To mark a gap in that context, we detect silent intervals directly in a ~ \tilde{a} using 5 ms frames, a threshold 70 dB below the track peak, and a minimum duration of 50 ms. If several intervals qualify, we choose the longest with audio on both sides. On the test sets, this detector finds the silenced interval in 99.9% of cuts, and both boundaries are within 10 ms of the true boundaries for 99.2% of TalkVid cuts and 99.6% of VoxMM cuts. Section D.8 examines gaps that are not digital silence and are filled instead with room tone or comfort noise. The interval is represented in c c by a placeholder and its duration, as illustrated in Fig. 5 .
blocks.zh: 读唇器R R将视觉Auto-AVSR[35]应用到整个窗口的口腔作物上. Beam 搜索返回其 N = 10 N = 10 最佳区分记录。 对于西班牙语和法语,我们使用马等人的读者[36]代替. Whisper big-v3 translators a ~\tilde{a} 提供可听的上下文 c c. 为了标出上下文的空白,我们用5ms帧、轨迹峰值以下的70dB阈值和50ms的最低持续时间,在~\tilde{a}中直接检测到无声间隔。 如果几个间隔符合条件,我们选择两侧有音频最长的间隔. 在测试机组上,这个探测器在99.9%的切片中发现静态间隔,对于99.2%的TalkVid切片和99.6%的VoxMM切片来说,两个边界都在10ms以内. D.8节审查不是数字沉默,而是用房间语气或舒适噪音填补的空白。 如图5所示,cc中以占位符及其持续时间表示间隔。

blocks.en: Figure 5 : A prompt of the language model and its answer (in bold) for a TalkVid test cut whose silenced words are “candle out”. No hypothesis contains these words. The model names the closest one and rewrites it using the context.

blocks.en: L L is Gemma-4 12B [ 52 ] (instruction-tuned), adapted with LoRA [ 26 ] of rank 32 ( α = 64 \alpha=64 , dropout 0.1) on the query, key, value and output projections of every attention layer. It is trained on English TalkVid windows only, with an effective batch of 16 (four samples and four accumulation steps) and a cosine learning-rate schedule, in three stages. In the first stage (3,000 steps, learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} ) the model learns to name the best candidate or to write the transcript. In the second (3,000 steps, 5 ⋅ 10 − 5 5\cdot 10^{-5} ) it learns the answer described in Sec. 4.2 , which names the best candidate and then edits it. In the third (1,000 steps, 5 ⋅ 10 − 5 5\cdot 10^{-5} ) noisy examples are added to the silenced ones. The hypotheses shown during training come from four readers: Auto-AVSR on the original video (50% of the examples), Auto-AVSR on mouth crops downscaled from 96 to 24 pixels and scaled back up (15%), Auto-AVSR on video in which half of the frames are replaced by the preceding frame (15%), and AV-HuBERT [ 50 ] (20%). The number of hypotheses shown is drawn uniformly between 1 and N N . At test time we decode greedily.
blocks.zh: LL是Gemma-4 12B [52](指令调试),与32级(α=64\alpha=64,退出0.1)的LORA[26]在查询,密钥,值和输出预测每个关注层上进行调整. 它只接受英语TalkVid窗口培训,有效批次为16个(4个样本和4个积分步骤)和3个阶段的余弦学习率表. 在第一阶段(3000步,学习率10−4 10^{-4}),模型学习指定最佳候选人或写抄本. 在第二步(3000步,5 ⋅ 10− 5 \ 5\cdot 10^{ 5})中,它学习了第4.2节中描述的答案,其中将最佳候选人命名,然后编辑. 在第三步(1000步,5 ~ 10 ~ 5 (5)\cdot 10~ 5 })中,吵闹的例子被添加到沉默的例中. 培训期间的假设来自四个读者: 原视频上的Auto-AVSR(50%的例子),口稼上的Auto-AVSR从96像素降低到24像素并缩放(15%),视频上的Auto-AVSR,其中一半帧被前帧(15%)取代,AV-HuBERT [50](20%). 显示的假设数在 1 和 N N 之间统一绘制 。 测试时我们贪婪地解码

blocks.en: For the ablation of Tab. 5 c, a small head reads AV-HuBERT [ 50 ] mouth features and passes its viseme posteriors to L L as soft input tokens. It is trained jointly with L L . To check that the model uses these features, we replace them at test time with the features of another clip. On the 360 verified validation cuts, the exact recovery of R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G then falls from 64.4% to 41.7% ( − 22.8 -22.8 , CI [ − 28.4 , − 17.2 ] [-28.4,-17.2] ).
blocks.zh: 为 a塔卜. 5c,一个小头读AV-HuBERT[50]口腔特征,并将它的粘液后质传递到LL作为软输入符号. 与LL联合培训。 为了检查模型是否使用了这些特性,我们在测试时用另一个剪辑的特性来代替它们. 在经过核实的360次验证削减中,R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G的确切回收率从64.4%下降到41.7%(−22.8-22.8, CI [−28.4,−17.2] [28.4-17.2]).

blocks.en: G G is the 22B-parameter LTX-2.5 transformer [ 21 ] , adapted with LoRA of rank 64 ( α = 64 \alpha=64 ) on the audio self-attention, the audio text cross-attention, the audio feed-forward layers and the video-to-audio attention. The video pathway is left unchanged. It is trained with AdamW [ 34 ] at a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} and a batch size of 2 on one H100 GPU, on English, Spanish and French TalkVid, in three stages. The first stage (5,000 steps) uses about 15,800 silenced spans of one to ten words, each given the lip reader’s transcript. The second (3,000 steps) uses 13,018 samples, one silenced and one noisy version of each of 6,509 windows from about 1,350 videos. Here the noisy samples receive the task tag without a transcript. Noisy training samples are mixed with babble, the seen sound effects, colored noise or a competing speaker at a signal-to-noise ratio drawn uniformly between − 15 -15 and 5 5 dB, sometimes with a second source 5 dB weaker. The third stage (2,000 steps) uses the same samples but varies the text given with the noisy ones: the lip reader’s transcript for half of them, the reference transcript for a quarter and no transcript for the rest. The generator thus learns to treat the transcript as a fallible hint and to work without one. The text is dropped for 10% of all samples, which trains the unconditional branch used for classifier-free guidance. The loss weight inside the silenced region is λ = 12 \lambda=12 , applied up to 60 ms beyond its edges. At inference we use 30 denoising steps with a fixed seed, and text guidance of 5 with <inpaint> and 1 with <denoise> . The generator produces the whole window: the audio outside the damaged region is generated together with the restored part, not copied from the input, and every score is computed on the generated window. Section D.6 shows that this leaves the intelligibility of intact speech unchanged.
blocks.zh: 一般事务人员 G是22B参数的LTX-2.5变压器[21],在音频自留心(α = 64\alpha = 64),音频文本横切,音频向导层和视频到音频的注意度上与64级的LORA相适应. 视频路径保持不变。 它与AdamW[34]一起接受培训,学习率为10 - 4 10 - 4 - 4 ,在英语、西班牙语和法语TalkVid上,分三个阶段对一个H100 GPU进行批量规模为2。 第一阶段(5,000步)使用大约15,800个1至10个字的消音段,每个段都给出了读唇的文字记录。 第二部(3000步)使用13,018个样本,从大约1,350个视频中,每个6,509个窗口有一个沉默和吵闹的版本. 在这里,吵闹的样本在没有记录的情况下收到任务标记. 噪声训练样品与bulble混合,可见的音效,彩色噪声或相竞的扬声器在−15-15和5 5 dB之间统一划出信号对噪比,有时出现第二个源5 dB弱. 第三阶段(2 000步)使用相同的样本,但与噪音的样本不同:一半的读唇语者记录稿,四分之一的参考记录稿,其余的则没有记录稿。 因此,生成者学会了把记录稿当作一个错误的暗示来对待,并且在没有记录的情况下工作。 文本被丢弃到所有样本的10%,它训练用于无分类器引导的无条件分支. 静态区域内部的损失重量为 QQ = 12\lambda = 12,施药量超过其边缘60 ms. 推断出,我们使用30个带固定种子的除音步骤,5个的文字指导用 "inpaint " ,1个的文字指导用 " denoise " 。 生成器产生整个窗口:受损区域以外的音频与恢复的部分一起生成,而不是从输入中复制,每个分数都计算在生成的窗口上. D.6节显示,这使完整无缺的言语的通晓性保持不变。

blocks.en: At inference, G G receives the video, the damaged track, a transcript of the whole window and the task tag. It is given neither the position nor the length of the damage, as a mask, as timestamps or as a marker in its text, and has to find by itself where speech is missing and where it must be kept. The same holds under noise: no component is told which part of a window is corrupted or how strongly, and the selection decides from the evidence alone ( Appendix C ). The only place where the location of a gap is used is the audible context of the language model. There, a silent interval is marked by a placeholder and its duration, because a recognizer such as Whisper does not report where words are missing from its transcript. The same detection also sets the task tag, <inpaint> when a silent interval is found and <denoise> otherwise. This detection step is a front end that can be replaced without changing the rest of the pipeline. Section D.8 already replaces it with a detector that uses both the audio and the lips, with nothing else changed. A recognizer that marks where it hears no speech, or that reports a confidence for each word, could supply the placeholder directly.
blocks.zh: 推论,G G接收视频,损坏的音轨,整个窗口的记录和任务标记. 它既不被赋予位置,也不被赋予破坏的长度,作为面具,时间戳或文字上的标记,它必须自己找到语言缺失的地方和必须保存的地方. 噪音下也有同样的情况:没有告知窗口的哪一部分被损坏或损坏程度如何,选择仅由证据决定(附录C)。 唯一使用空隙位置的地方是语言模型的可听性上下文. 在那里,静默的间隔用一个占位符及其持续时间来标记,因为像Whisper这样的识别器不报告其记录中缺少文字的地方. 同样的检测还设置了任务标记, 当找到无声间隔时的“ inpaint” 和“ denoise” 否则。 这个检测步骤是一个前端,可以在不改变管道其余部分的情况下进行替换. D.8节已经用一个既使用音频又使用嘴唇的探测器来取代它,没有其他变化. 一个识别器,如果它听到没有讲话,或者它报告对每个字的信任,可以直接为占位符提供标记.

blocks.en: B.2 Resources and runtime
blocks.zh: B.2 资源和运行时间

blocks.en: All training and inference runs use one NVIDIA H100 GPU with 80 GB of memory per job. The generator’s 22B-parameter backbone stays frozen in bfloat16, and only its adapters are trained. We encode the training windows’ audio and video latents once in advance. A generator training step with batch size 2 then takes about 2 s, and its three stages take about 6 GPU-hours in total. The language model takes about 2.5 s per step on one GPU, or about 5 GPU-hours across its three stages. At inference, one 30-step generation of a 4.8 s speech window takes about 11 s. A fixed configuration requires one pass. Selection requires one pass for each configuration, six for a damaged window and three when no speech is audible. Each distinct resulting transcript is then scored by Whisper and the lip reader with both the real and uninformative inputs ( Appendix C ).
blocks.zh: 所有训练和推论运行都使用一个NVIDIA H100 GPU,每个工作有80GB的内存. 发电机的22B参数主干件在bfloat16中被冻结,只有它的适配器经过训练. 我们事先将训练窗口的音频和视频潜伏编码一次。 分批2的发电机训练步骤则需要大约2s,其三个阶段总共需要大约6GPU小时. 语言模型在一个GPU上每步需要2.5s左右,或者在它的三个阶段上大约需要5GPU小时. 推论,一个30步的一代4.8s语音窗口大约需要11s. 固定配置需要一次通过. 选择每个配置需要1个传球,一个损坏的窗口需要6个传球,没有语音时需要3个传球. 之后,Whisper和唇语阅读器会用真实的和不真实的输入(附录C)来打分。

blocks.en: Both terms in Eq. 2 are teacher-forced log-likelihoods of each candidate transcript, summed over tokens. The audio term e A e_{A} uses Whisper large-v3 to score the transcript conditioned first on the damaged input a ~ \tilde{a} and then on a silent track of equal length. The visual term e R e_{R} uses visual Auto-AVSR’s weighted attention and CTC log-likelihoods ( 0.9 0.9 and 0.1 0.1 , its decoder weights), conditioned first on the window’s mouth crops and then on a repetition of its first crop. The repeated crop retains the speaker’s appearance while removing articulation. If the generator produces no speech, its empty transcript receives no evidence, does not vote, and cannot be selected. When USR 2.0 replaces Auto-AVSR as the lip reader, only the hypotheses of R R change. The evidence terms are computed as above, and the audio-visual hypotheses for noisy input still come from Auto-AVSR, so the swap needs no retraining and no new setting.

blocks.en: Each term is normalized against its own baseline. Subtracting the same recognizer’s log-likelihood of the same transcript under an uninformative input largely cancels the recognizer’s language prior and the cost of the transcript’s length. What remains is an estimate of the pointwise mutual information between the transcript and the input. Both terms are therefore log-likelihood ratios in the same unit, and we sum them without a modality weight: a modality that carries no word information gives a value near zero for every candidate and drops out. We sum over tokens rather than average, so that a transcript supported word by word outweighs one supported by a single confident word. Every window has the same length, which keeps this scale comparable across clips. The only global scale is the temperature T T .
blocks.zh: 每个任期按照自己的基线正常化。 在非信息性输入下将同一识别器对同一记录记录的相似性进行切换,在很大程度上取消了识别器在记录之前的语言和记录长度的费用。 剩下的是对笔录和输入之间的点性相互信息的估计。 因此,这两个术语都是同一单位的对数相似比率,我们将它们汇总而无模式权重:一种没有字词信息的方式给每个候选人一个接近零的值,然后退出。 我们用符号而不是平均数字来归纳,这样,一个字支持的文字记录就超过一个字支持的文字记录。 每一个窗口的长度都是一样的,这使得这个比例尺度在剪辑之间保持可比性. 唯一的全球尺度是温度T T.

Allowing both to vote would count that information twice. When y ^ L \hat{y}_{L} votes, we therefore retain the configuration that speaks h 1 h_{1} over silence as a candidate but exclude it as a voter. blocks.en: Table 12 gives the WER behind Fig. 4 for the selection, every fixed configuration and the two text outputs. The averages quoted in Sec. 5.3 are its last column, with the input audio kept for the fixed configurations. No fixed configuration is best in every condition. Those that keep the audio lead while speech remains audible, but they fail under whole-clip − 20 -20 dB babble, where the same configurations over silence are far better. The selection adapts to both cases: it keeps the audio while speech is audible and switches to the configurations over silence when the babble covers the whole clip. Under whole-clip − 20 -20 dB babble it stays within about a point of the muted configurations and of the lip reader’s own text, without being told the noise level. The muted rows of Tab. 12 are reference rows that are given the damaged region and replace only that region with silence, which is why they repeat the silence columns. The selection does not receive the damaged region. Its muted candidates discard the whole input track, and it chooses between them and the candidates that keep the audio using the evidence alone. Even so, it matches or improves on the muted rows in every condition except whole-clip − 20 -20 dB babble, where it is within half a point.

blocks.en: The fixed configurations in Tab. 12 use one choice for every input. For a stronger retrospective comparator, we choose the lowest-WER configuration separately for each condition using that condition’s test outcomes. It therefore knows the condition and the results, and its muted configurations also know the damaged region, but it still uses one configuration for every sample in that condition. The per-sample oracle of Tab. 10 is a different comparator. Under Whisper scoring, selection outperforms this condition-wise rule on both the noisy set and the condition grid ( Tab. 11 a). Five configurations lead across the grid’s 13 conditions, including G G alone on clean input and muted configurations under − 20 -20 dB babble.

On those disagreement subsets, its choice has substantially lower WER than equal-weight voting ( Tab. 11 b). This conditional analysis explains why evidence can matter for individual inputs while the aggregate difference in Tab. 10 is modest.

blocks.en: We first examine paired comparisons with the baselines, then test whether the noisy-speech results hold across interference sources and test sets. The remaining analyses probe the generator, the scoring protocol, examples of the recovered speech, gaps that are not digital silence, and what the language model takes from the lip reader.
blocks.zh: 我们首先检查与基线的配对比较,然后测试噪音-声波结果是否跨越干扰源和测试集。 剩下的分析探索了生成器,评分协议,恢复语音的例子,不是数字沉默的漏洞,以及语言模型从读唇器那里得到的.

blocks.en: D.1 Comparison with the baselines
blocks.zh: D.1 与基线的比较

blocks.en: With Auto-AVSR as the lip reader, our method significantly exceeds every baseline except USR 2.0, with which it is statistically tied on the pooled cuts ( Tab. 13 a). The comparison varies by test set: our lead over USR 2.0 is 6.9 points on TalkVid (CI [ 0.5 , 13.2 ] [0.5,13.2] ) but 1.2 on VoxMM (CI [ − 4.6 , 7.0 ] [-4.6,7.0] ). On VoxMM, the difference from Llama-AVSR also includes zero ( + 6.2 +6.2 , CI [ − 0.4 , 11.9 ] [-0.4,11.9] ).
blocks.zh: 以Auto-AVSR为读唇器,我们的方法大大超过除USR 2.0以外的每个基线,而USR 2.0在统计上与集合削减挂钩(Tab.13a)。 比较因测试组合而异:我们比USR 2.0的领先点是TalkVid(CI [0.5, 13.2] [0.5,13.2])的6.9分,但比VoxMM(CI [−4.6, 7.0][-4.6,7.0])的1.2分. 关于VoxMM,与Llama-AVSR的区别还包括0分(+6.2+6.2,CI [−0.4, 11.9] [-0.4,11.9])。

blocks.en: USR 2.0 is a stronger lip reader than Auto-AVSR. Substituting it for Auto-AVSR raises our exact recovery from 39.3% to 43.8% ( + 4.5 +4.5 , CI [ 1.1 , 7.7 ] [1.1,7.7] ), 8.0 points (CI [ 5.3 , 11.0 ] [5.3,11.0] ) above USR 2.0 alone.
blocks.zh: 美国 2.0是比Auto-AVSR更强的读唇器. 以Auto-AVSR代替它,将我们的准确回收率从39.3%提高到43.8%(+4.5+4.5, CI [1.1, 7.7] [1.1,7.7]),8.0分(CI [5.3, 11.0] [5.3,11.0]),仅高于USR 2.0。

blocks.en: Averaged over the five conditions, our method has significantly lower WER than every baseline ( Tab. 13 b). No baseline is significantly better on any pooled condition, although three are tied with it on one condition each.
blocks.zh: 平均而言,在五个条件下,我们的方法大大低于每个基线(表13b)。 在任何集合条件下,基线都无比好得多,不过有三个与基线挂钩,每个条件只有一个。

blocks.en: Which baseline comes closest to our method depends on the type of interference. VisualVoice matches our competing-speaker result on the windows it covers ( + 1.6 +1.6 , CI [ − 0.8 , 4.0 ] [-0.8,4.0] ) and is better on VoxMM alone ( + 3.9 +3.9 , CI [ 0.8 , 6.9 ] [0.8,6.9] ). USR 2.0 using only the lips ties with us under − 10 -10 dB babble ( − 3.5 -3.5 , CI [ − 7.5 , 0.6 ] [-7.5,0.6] ), where audio is least informative. USR 2.0 using lips and audio ties under − 5 -5 dB babble ( − 0.6 -0.6 , CI [ − 4.5 , 2.6 ] [-4.5,2.6] ), where much speech remains audible.
blocks.zh: 哪个基线最接近我们的方法 取决于干扰的类型 视觉 声音与我们所覆盖的窗户(+1.6+1.6、CI [− 0.8、4.0][-0.8、4.0])的相匹配,仅VoxMM就更好(+ 3.9+3.9、CI [0.8、6.9] [0.8、6.9] )。 USR 2.0使用嘴唇和声带在−5-5 dB babble(−0.6-0.6,CI [−4.5,2.6] [-4.5,2.6])下,其中很多话语仍然可以发声.

blocks.en: Replacing our lip reader with USR 2.0 reduces average WER from 27.2% to 25.5% ( − 1.7 -1.7 , CI [ − 3.1 , − 0.2 ] [-3.1,-0.2] ). The babble comparison is repeated with other recordings in Sec. D.2 .
blocks.zh: 用USR 2.0取代我们的读唇器将平均WER从27.2%减少到25.5%(−1.7-1.7,CI [−3.1,−0.2] [-3.1,-0.2])。 与Sec.D.2中的其他录音重复了比对。

blocks.en: We also run SAM Audio on the pooled TalkVid and VoxMM noisy samples, using “speech” as the text prompt or the masked target-speaker video as the visual prompt. Both variants have substantially higher average WER than our method with either output transcriber ( Tab. 13 b and Tab. 20 ). SAM Audio is also evaluated on the hard set in Tab. 14 .
blocks.zh: 我们还在集合TalkVid和VoxMM的噪音样本上运行SAM Audio,使用“speech”作为文字提示,或使用遮蔽的目标语视频作为视觉提示。 这两个变体的平均WER值都比我们采用输出转录法(Tab. 13 b和Tab. 20)的方法要高得多。 萨姆 音频也在Tab 14的硬盘上进行评估。

blocks.en: F5-TTS and AlignDiT, both given our language model’s transcript and the span location, are statistically tied with us. Much of the gain on this set comes from the language model ( Tab. 5 a), whose transcript these editors also use. For noisy speech, our method significantly improves on every baseline except VisualVoice. Its face detector succeeds on fewer than half of the windows, and the two methods tie on that subset.
blocks.zh: F5-TTS和AlignDIT, 既考虑到我们语言模型的笔录, 也考虑到跨度位置, 本集的大部分收益来自语言模型(Tab. 5 a),这些编辑也使用其笔录. 除了Visual Voice之外,我们的方法在每一个基线上都有很大的改进。 它的面部探测器在不到一半的窗口上成功,两种方法在那个子集上捆绑.

blocks.en: D.2 Babble from other recordings
blocks.zh: D.2 其他录音

blocks.en: The main evaluation uses DEMAND cafeteria babble on microphone channels held out from training ( Sec. A.2 ). To examine other babble, we test the same speech windows with two further sources. One is DEMAND’s restaurant scene, recorded in a different room and session. The other sums speech from six talkers in six held-out test videos, excluding the source video of each window. Neither source shares a recording, scene, or speaker with training. We replace the babble in all 546 samples at both levels from Tab. 3 , keeping the video, clean speech, generator text, sampling seed, and mixing code fixed. Only the interference and its mixing level change.
blocks.zh: 主要评价是使用培训后保持的麦克风频道(Sec.A.2.)上的DENAND自助餐厅泡泡。 为了检查其他的bulble,我们用另外两个来源测试同一个语音窗口. 一个是DEAND的餐厅场景, 其他总和是六个演讲者在六个悬疑测试视频中的演讲,不包括每个窗口的源视频. 无论是录音、现场还是演讲, 我们更换了塔布所有546个样本中的泡泡 3,保留视频,清真语音,发电机文字,采样种子,混合码固定. 只有干扰及其混合水平变化。

blocks.en: At a fixed signal-to-noise ratio, different babble recordings need not mask speech equally. The cafeteria recording has 39% of its energy between 300 and 3,400 Hz, compared with 69% for the restaurant recording. At the nominal − 5 -5 dB level, restaurant babble and the six-talker mixture raise noisy-input WER from 52.9% to above 90%. A comparison at the same ratio would therefore confound babble source with input difficulty. Instead, we choose ratios that match Whisper’s noisy-input WER under cafeteria babble: − 5.4 -5.4 and − 1.4 -1.4 dB for the restaurant, and − 4.6 -4.6 and − 0.4 -0.4 dB for the six talkers. We fix these ratios using only the noisy inputs, before running any restoration method. At each level, input WER then differs from the cafeteria condition by at most 1.3 points ( Tab. 15 , first row).
blocks.zh: 在固定的信号对噪音比例下,不同的bulble录音不需要同样遮掩语音. 食堂记录的能量有39%在300到3 400之间 Hz,与69%的餐厅录音相比. 在名义上的− 5-5 dB 级,餐厅的bulble 和6个谈话者的混合物将噪音输入WER从52.9%提高到90%以上. 因此,如果以同样的比例进行比较,就会使泡泡源与输入困难相混淆。 相反,我们选择了与Whisper在食堂大呼小叫下高声输入WER的比例: − 5.4 - 5.4 和 − 1.4 - 1.4 dB 的餐厅, − 4.6 - 4.6 和 − 0.4 dB 的六个说话者。 在使用任何恢复方法之前,我们只使用噪音输入来修正这些比率。 在每个关卡,输入WER随即与食堂条件不同,最多为1.3分(Tab. 15,第一行).

blocks.en: For each new mixture, we regenerate the three configurations that use the input audio and rerun selection with the same rule and temperature, recomputing only its input-dependent evidence. We also rerun DeepFilterNet3, Sidon, and VisualVoice with their original code. LipVoicer and AlignDiT do not use the input audio ( Tab. 7 ), so their outputs are identical across babble sources. As a reproducibility check, rerunning our cafeteria-babble outputs on a second cluster changes WER by no more than 0.1 points.
blocks.zh: 对于每种新的混合物,我们重新生成使用输入音频的三种配置,并以相同的规则和温度重新运行选择,只重新计算其输入依赖性的证据. 我们还重新运行 DeepFilterNet3, Sidon, 和Visual Voice 的原始代码. LipVoicer和AlignDiT不使用输入音频(Tab. 7),因此其输出在bable源之间是相同的. 作为可复制性的检查,在第二组中重新运行我们的自助餐厅-泡泡产出,对WER的修改不超过0.1分.

blocks.en: Our method’s WER remains comparable across the cafeteria and the two independent babble sources ( Tab. 15 ). Relative to cafeteria babble, the restaurant difference is + 0.0 +0.0 (CI [ − 1.7 , 1.7 ] [-1.7,1.7] ) and the six-talker difference is + 1.2 +1.2 (CI [ − 0.1 , 2.5 ] [-0.1,2.5] ). Neither is significant, also when the two levels are considered separately. Our method remains significantly ahead of every baseline evaluated here for both new sources, with similar margins and the same baseline ordering. Under restaurant babble, none of its fixed configurations changes significantly either.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法WER在食堂和两个独立的babble来源(Tab. 15)之间仍然具有可比性。 相对于食堂泡泡,餐厅差异为+0.0+0.0(CI [−1.7,1.7] [1.7,1.7]),六对讲机差异为+1.2+1.2(CI [−0.1,2.5] [-0.1,2.5]),两者的差别也不显著,当两个级别分别考虑时也是如此. 我们的方法仍然大大领先于在此评估的对两个新来源的每一个基准,其幅度和基线顺序相似。 在餐厅的胡言乱语下,其固定配置也没有显著改变.

blocks.en: The six-talker mixture is harder for several audio-processing methods despite the matched input WER. DeepFilterNet3 and Sidon both lose significantly. Among our fixed configurations, G G alone is affected most, whereas the configurations given a transcript rise far less. The selection limits the effect by muting the input on 30% of these windows, compared with 25% under cafeteria babble, and hence relying more on the lips when the audio is harder to restore. Its margin over DeepFilterNet3 grows as a result.
blocks.zh: 尽管有匹配的输入WER,但几种音频处理方法的六对讲机混合物更为困难. DeepFilterNet3和西顿都损失惨重. 在我们的固定配置中,仅GG就受影响最大,而提供记录片的配置上升幅度要小得多。 选择通过对30%的这些窗口的输入进行调音来限制效果,而食堂bulble下为25%,因此在音频难以恢复时更多地依赖唇. 它在DeepFilterNet3上的比值因此增长.

blocks.en: We also test restaurant babble at the main experiment’s nominal − 10 -10 and − 5 -5 dB. This is a harder input condition: noisy-input WER increases from 72.3% to 95.0%. Output WER rises for every method, including R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G at 51.0% and DeepFilterNet3 at 95.0%. Their relative difference remains comparable to that under cafeteria babble ( − 44.0 -44.0 , CI [ − 52.4 , − 36.7 ] [-52.4,-36.7] , versus − 42.4 -42.4 ).
blocks.zh: 我们还在主要实验名义上的 - 10 - 10 和 - 5 - 5 dB 测试餐厅的泡泡。 这是一个更硬的输入条件:噪音输入WER从72.3%增加到95.0%. 每种方法的输出WER都上升,包括R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G为51.0%,DeepFilterNet3为95.0%. 它们之间的相对差异仍然与食堂泡泡(−44.0-44.0,CI[−52.4,−36.7][-52.4,-36.7],相对于−42.4-42.4)相似。

blocks.zh: D.3 每个测试集的噪音发言

blocks.en: Table 16 disaggregates Tab. 3 by test set. WER is higher on VoxMM even for the clean recordings, and the lip readers alone are about twice as wrong there as on TalkVid. These differences help explain why every method performs worse on VoxMM.
blocks.zh: 表16按测试组分列了表3。 WER在VoxMM上甚至对于干净的录音来说都更高,光是唇形读物就比TalkVid上错误的两倍左右. 这些差异有助于解释为什么每一种方法在VoxMM上表现更糟糕.

blocks.en: Our method has the lowest average WER on both sets. The two sets differ most under − 10 -10 dB babble, the condition in which performance relies most on the lip reader. There, replacing Auto-AVSR with USR 2.0 in our pipeline hardly changes the result on TalkVid but lowers the WER by six points on VoxMM.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法在两套中的平均WER最低. 两套在−10-10 dB babble下差异最大,表现最依赖于唇读器的条件. 在那里,在我们的管道中用USR 2.0取代Auto-AVSR 几乎改变不了TalkVid的结果,而是将WER在VoxMM上降低6点.

blocks.en: Figure 7 breaks the silenced results down by the number of silenced words. Every configuration recovers fewer spans as the span grows. The language model improves on the lip reader, and the generator speaking its transcript improves further at every length, from 59.2% for the lip reader to 72.5% for single words and from 16.7% to 23.7% for seven to ten words. The generator contributes most for single words: there, speaking the lip reader’s best hypothesis ( R → G R\rightarrow G ) already recovers clearly more spans than that hypothesis itself, whereas for seven to ten words the two are within a point. The selection adds about two points to R → L → G R\rightarrow L\rightarrow G for spans of up to three words and matches it for longer ones.
blocks.zh: 图7用沉默字数打破沉默结果。 每一个配置的恢复间隔随着跨度的增加而减少. 语言模型在读唇器上有所改进,发声器在每一个长度上都有进一步的改进,从读唇器的59.2%到单词的72.5%,从16.7%到7到10个单词的23.7%. 生成器对单个词的贡献最大:在那里,说读唇者的最佳假设(R ~ G R\rightarrow G)已经比假设本身恢复了更清晰的跨度,而对于7到10个词来说,两者在一个点之内。 选择为 R → L → G R\ 右旋 L\ 右旋 G 添加了约 2 个点,其跨度可达 3 个字,与之相匹配为更长的词.

blocks.en: D.5 Generator controls
blocks.zh: D.5 发电机控制

blocks.en: The following controls examine how the generator responds to the supplied text and video.
blocks.zh: 以下控制检查生成器如何响应所提供的文本和视频.

blocks.en: To isolate the generator’s contribution, we give G G the window’s reference transcript in place of L L ’s transcript. Whisper then recovers the silenced span exactly in more than 95% of the verified cuts of every set, including the hard set ( Tab. 17 a), and this holds for spans of five to ten words (95.8% on TalkVid and VoxMM). Given the same reference transcript, every speech editor recovers fewer spans on every set, although the editors are also given the span’s location. G G also remains the highest on the 108 hard-set cuts that every method covers. These oracle-text results show that the generator usually places and speaks the supplied words intelligibly, even when the mouth is difficult to read, so most remaining errors of the full pipeline arise before generation. They also help explain why a stronger lip reader improves results without retraining ( Sec. D.1 ).
blocks.zh: 为了分离发电机的贡献,我们把G的参考笔录代替LL的笔录。 然后Whisper恢复了每套中95%以上经核实的剪切时间段,包括硬盘(Tab.17 a),这段时间为5至10个字(TalkVid和VoxMM上为95.8%)。 由于同样的参考记录,每个演讲编辑在每集中恢复的时间间隔都比较短,尽管编辑们也得到了时间间隔的位置。 GG在每种方法覆盖的108个硬定切片中也保持最高. 这些oracle-text的结果表明,生成器通常会将所供应的单词放置和说得通,即使嘴部难以读取,因此大部分完整的管道剩余的错误都会在生成前出现. 它们也有助于解释为什么一个更强的唇形读物在不进行再培训的情况下会提高效果(第D.1节)。

blocks.en: The generator also follows the supplied transcript under noise ( Tab. 17 b). Given the noisy input and the reference transcript, G G lowers the WER of our selection on every set, by about half when pooled, and on TalkVid and VoxMM it comes within about three points of the clean recordings ( Tab. 16 ). The hard set shows the same pattern, with the WER halving.

blocks.en: If G G only spoke the text it is given, the lips it sees would not matter. We test this by changing only its video input. For each eligible sample, the replacement is the nearest nonoverlapping segment of the same source video that contains none of the target content words. Stop words and fillers are ignored for this exclusion. Both segments come from the same source video, and as an additional screen against other speakers we require a WavLM-Base-plus-SV speaker cosine of at least 0.86. The audio, the supplied transcript, the sampling seed and all inference settings are kept, and the replacement lips still move, so the intervention changes what the lips say and little else. A third input removes the articulation altogether: a frozen mouth, in which the first frame of the window is repeated over its whole length, as in the baseline of the visual evidence e R e_{R} . This third input lets us separate what the correct lips add from what conflicting lips cost. The experiment covers every sample with an eligible replacement: 1,877 of the 2,092 verified silenced cuts, and 914 severe-noise samples, in which babble at − 10 -10 or − 20 -20 dB covers four words or the whole window. To measure the variation between two renders, we also generate 300 samples of each task again with their own video.
blocks.zh: 如果G只说它给出的文字,它看到的唇就不重要了. 我们只通过改变视频输入来测试它。 对于每个符合条件的样本,替换是同一源视频中最接近的不重叠部分,没有包含目标内容单词. 停止的单词和填充符会被忽略为此排除. 两段都来自同一源视频,作为对其他发言者的附加屏幕,我们需要至少0.86的WavLM-Base-plus-SV扬声器余弦. 音频,提供的语录,采样种子和所有推论设置都保留下来,替换的嘴唇仍然在移动,所以干预会改变嘴唇所说的话,其他的也很少. 第三个输入完全去除了表达:一个冷冻的口,其中窗口的第一帧在整个长度上重复,如视觉证据e R e_{R}的基线. 这第三个输入让我们把正确的嘴唇加上什么与冲突的嘴唇的代价分开. 实验用合格的替代物覆盖每个样本:2,092个经核实的静音切片中的1,877个,以及914个严重噪音样本,其中在−10-10或−20-20 dB处的泡泡覆盖4个字或整个窗口. 为了衡量两者的差异,我们还用他们自己的视频再次生成300个任务样本。

blocks.en: With the transcript held fixed, a frozen mouth lowers exact recovery at every span length and raises WER in every severe-noise condition, and mismatched lips cost more again ( Tab. 18 ). In these columns the transcript is still the one obtained from the correct lips, so the lip reader and the language model play no part in either loss, and both arise in the generator itself. The loss with a frozen mouth shows that the correct lips help the generator beyond the words it is given. The additional loss with mismatched lips shows that it follows those words less faithfully when the lips contradict them. Over all cuts and over all severe-noise samples, mismatched lips are also significantly worse than the frozen mouth. The effect of the lips is largest under severe noise. When babble at − 20 -20 dB covers the whole clip, the generator voices the supplied transcript only with the correct video, and fails with a frozen mouth as completely as with mismatched lips. Two renders of the same sample with its own video differ by at most 0.1 points, so none of these differences is sampling variation.
blocks.zh: 随着记录的固定,冰冻的口腔会降低每一间间距的准确恢复,并在每一次严重噪声条件下提高WER,不匹配的嘴唇成本会更高(表18)。 在这些栏目中,笔录仍然是从正确的嘴唇中获取的,所以唇读器和语言模型在任何一种损失中都没有作用,两者都出现在生成器本身. 结冰口的损耗表明,正确的嘴唇帮助生成者超越它给出的文字. 双唇不匹配造成的额外损失表明,当双唇与双唇相矛盾时,双唇不忠实地遵循这些词语。 在所有切口和所有严重噪声样本中,不匹配的嘴唇也明显比冰冻的嘴更糟糕. 在强烈的噪音下,唇的效果最大. 当在 − 20 - 20 dB 时, 生成器只用正确的视频来声音提供的记录, 并且与不匹配的嘴唇完全一样, 无法用冷冻的嘴。 两个用自己的视频制作的相同样本在最多0.1点上存在差异,所以这些差异都不是采样变异.

blocks.en: Without a transcript, the generator depends on the lips wherever it has something to recover. A frozen mouth halves its recovery on short spans, and mismatched lips remove more. Longer spans are near zero even with the correct video, and whole-window − 20 -20 dB babble is already beyond G G alone, so neither can fall further. When the lip reader also reads the mismatched lips, the loss under severe noise grows again ( + 40.9 +40.9 points over all samples, CI [ 35.0 , 48.6 ] [35.0,48.6] ). The visual signal therefore enters the pipeline twice, through recognition and through generation.
blocks.zh: 没有笔录,生成器就取决于它的嘴唇,只要它有东西可以恢复。 冰冻的嘴在短短的时间内将恢复减半,不匹配的嘴唇会移除更多的. 更长的跨度甚至与正确的视频也接近于零,全窗 — 20-20 dB babble已经超越了G G单独,因此两者都无法进一步下降. 当读唇读音也读到不匹配的唇时,严重噪声下的损失会再次增加(在所有样本中,CI[35.0,48.6][35.0,48.6]),因此视觉信号通过识别和生成两次进入管道.
